slides.title: A pattern machine — not a mathematician
slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.
slides.lead: It predicts a useful next response from your brief and its training. It does not prove Pythagoras, know your class, or stand behind a grade.

items.title: Not a colleague
items.body: It has not taught your Year 9s. It does not remember who still confuses the hypotenuse.

items.title: Not a mark scheme
items.body: A fluent worked solution can still use a method you do not teach, or a step that is simply wrong.

items.title: You still decide
items.body: Whether it is correct, fair, on-curriculum, and fit for these students — that stays with you.

slides.remember: It does not prove Pythagoras. You still stand behind every line.

slides.title: Why fluent maths can still be wrong
slides.activity: Name the boundary. What stays with the teacher?
slides.lead: Confidence in the tone is not evidence. Check every line of mathematics before it reaches a class.

slides.title: What ChatGPT is actually for in maths
slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.
slides.lead: Use it as a drafting assistant for low-risk teacher work. You remain the editor and the mathematician.

items.title: Practice that you will check
items.body: Retrieval starters, exit tickets, worked-example fading, three versions of the same worksheet with the same objective.

items.title: Planning support
items.body: A first pass at a lesson sequence, a list of misconceptions, a Criterion B investigation scaffold — then you cut, correct and own it.

items.title: Words around the maths
items.body: A parent-friendly explanation of a method. Feedback stems. A first draft of an answer key you rework yourself.

slides.title: What it is not for
slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.
slides.lead: If it carries a name, a mark, or an unpublished assessment, it does not go in.

items.title: Assessment that counts
items.body: Unpublished unit tests. Live exam papers. Marks. Comments you will paste onto ManageBac as if they were yours.

items.title: People
items.body: Named students, photos of exercise books, SEN / IEP notes, parent threads, anything that identifies a child.

items.title: The figure itself
items.body: Accurate graphs, scaled diagrams, labelled geometry. That is Desmos, GeoGebra or the GDC — not an image generator.

items.title: Student work on their behalf
items.body: Do not ‘solve this homework’ for a child, or write the Criterion B they then submit as theirs.

items.title: Green — generally suitable
items.body: Public curriculum. Your own worksheet with no names. Past papers already public. ‘A Year 7 class’ as a fictional group.

items.title: Amber — pause
items.body: Unpublished unit plans. School-branded booklets. Class-level patterns that could still identify a small group. Check with the HoD.

items.title: Red — stop
items.body: Names + marks. Photos of work. Unpublished tests. SEN / medical / safeguarding. Parent disputes. Anything in ManageBac about a child.

slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.

items.title: Identity
items.body: A name, a photo, a distinctive seating plan, ‘the boy who arrived from X in March’.

items.title: Marks and comments
items.body: Spreadsheets, report drafts, criterion levels attached to a person.

items.title: Unpublished assessment
items.body: This week’s test, the mock, the investigation that has not been issued yet.

items.title: Special category
items.body: IEP, extra time, medical, pastoral. Do not ‘just test it’ with a real case.

slides.title: Brief it with SCOPE-V
slides.activity: Follow the sequence. This is the move you will reuse.
slides.lead: Brief it the way you would brief a colleague covering your class. ‘Make a fractions lesson’ is not a brief.

items.title: Situation
items.body: Year 9, first lesson back on Pythagoras, mixed prior knowledge, 50 minutes.

items.title: Constraints
items.body: MYP Criterion A. No student names. One projector. Calculators later, not in the starter.

items.title: Output
items.body: 8-minute retrieval: 4 questions increasing in demand, one misconception, answers on a separate key.

items.title: Persona
items.body: An IB MYP mathematics teacher. Short items. No invented methods.

items.title: Examples
items.body: Question 1 is a missing hypotenuse. Question 4 needs a decision: is this a right triangle?

items.title: Verify
items.body: Work every answer. Flag any method we do not teach. Do not invent a page of the IB guide.

slides.example: Year 9 Pythagoras, 8 minutes, four questions increasing in demand, one misconception, answers on a separate key you will work. That is a brief.

slides.title: Differentiation is not ‘make it easy’
slides.activity: Name the boundary. What stays with the teacher?
slides.lead: Keep the learning objective. Change the access, not the ambition.

slides.title: Generated images versus mathematical figures
slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.
slides.lead: ChatGPT can sketch a mood. It cannot be trusted with scale, a right-angle mark, a coordinate grid, or a labelled hypotenuse.

items.title: What image generation is for
items.body: A decorative hook on a slide. A scene that is not being measured. Never a figure students will read as true.

items.title: What it gets wrong
items.body: Right angles on the wrong vertex. Unequal ticks that look equal. Graphs that miss intercepts. Axes without scale.

items.title: The right tool
items.body: Desmos, GeoGebra or the GDC for graphs and constructions. Screenshot that. Put the screenshot on the slide or sheet.

slides.remember: If students will measure it, count on it, or copy it, it was not generated.

slides.title: Never trust a generated graph
slides.activity: Name the boundary. What stays with the teacher?
slides.lead: A picture that looks like y = x² is not a graph of y = x² until a tool that does mathematics drew it.
slides.avoidBody: Ask ChatGPT to ‘draw the graph of y = 2x + 1’ and paste it into a worksheet as the figure.
avoidBullets: Ask ChatGPT to ‘draw the graph of y = 2x + 1’ and paste it into a worksheet as the figure.
slides.aimBody: Plot it in Desmos or on the GDC. Screenshot. Crop. Add alt text. The mathematics came from a tool that graphs, not a tool that draws.
aimBullets: Plot it in Desmos or on the GDC. Screenshot. Crop. Add alt text. The mathematics came from a tool that graphs, not a tool that draws.

slides.title: When a screenshot is better than a drawing
slides.activity: Listen with the room — tick a point as you take it in.
slides.lead: Match the tool to the job. ChatGPT can still help with the words around the figure.

items.title: Graphs and loci
items.body: Desmos or GDC. Then ask ChatGPT for three questions about that graph — you still check the intercepts.

items.title: Geometry
items.body: GeoGebra or a careful sketch. Do not let a generated triangle teach the Pythagorean setup.

items.title: Uploaded photos of a board
items.body: A photo of your own board, no students in frame, can be a prompt for ‘list the steps I wrote’. Still check them.

A graph students will read values from — Desmos / GDC only.
